parameters.content:
## Versions API
The version history behind the job page. **Nothing here calls Claude.** The two that change data (`edit`, `restore`) first check the `X-JobHunter: 1` header, so a web page on another site cannot trigger them. Ids are checked as UUIDs inside the SQL before use. Every answer is quick (well under 30 s).

- `GET api/jobs/versions` the list, newest first
- `POST api/jobs/versions/edit` saves an edit as a new version (the code checks run again)
- `POST api/jobs/versions/restore` copies an old version as a new one

Versions are append-only: nothing here updates or deletes a `document_versions` row. A version must belong to the job in the query, or the answer is `404 version_not_found`.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments. The parameters are
-- substituted everywhere in the text, comments included, which breaks the query.
-- passed is the review's verdict, or null (not reviewed) when the review is not an object or carries
-- reviewedVersionNo: the reviewer is not run again on edits, so an edited version (and a restored copy of
-- one) has no verdict of its own.
with p as (select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as id),
j as (
  select jobs.id from jobs, p where jobs.id = p.id and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid
)
select exists (select 1 from j) as found,
  coalesce((
    select json_agg(json_build_object(
      'id', d.id, 'versionNo', d.version_no, 'label', d.label, 'origin', d.origin,
      'createdAt', to_char(d.created_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"'),
      'instruction', d.instruction,
      'passed', case when jsonb_typeof(d.review) <> 'object' or d.review ? 'reviewedVersionNo' then null
                     else coalesce((d.review -> 'passed') = 'true'::jsonb, false) end,
      'hardChecks', (select count(*) from jsonb_array_elements(case when jsonb_typeof(d.checks) = 'array' then d.checks else '[]'::jsonb end) c
                     where c ->> 'severity' = 'hard')::int,
      'manualEdit', d.manual_edit) order by d.version_no desc)
    from document_versions d join j on d.job_id = j.id), '[]'::json) as versions;

parameters.content:
## Edit
`POST api/jobs/versions/edit?id=` body `{ fromVersionId, cv, coverLetter }`, at most 200 KB (`413 too_large`, before anything else is called). Only the known CV and cover letter fields are kept, an empty location, email, phone, work rights or experience location becomes null (the same as every saved document). The worker checks it (`400 invalid_document {path}` for a missing or wrong-type field), exactly as the Generate workflow does: the job, the **current** base CV and base cover letter (their effective facts: Prayush's edits, else what was read from the file), the other jobs. The worker also lists the fields that differ from the source (`/generation/changed-paths`). `reasons.manualEdits` keeps his edits **by text**, `{ path, text }` (`null` text: a field he emptied): the source's edits where their text is now (path updated if it moved within its list; an old path-only row is read as the text at that path), plus every changed field whose text is new (a bullet that only moved is not an edit). A regenerate copies these exactly (they are locked).

Saved as a new version: `origin edited`, label `Edited`, `manual_edit` true, `parent_version_id` the source. The review is the source's, marked `reviewedVersionNo` (the reviewer does not run again). The checks run against the current base CV, while the saved version keeps the base CV it was written from (the page tells the user when the two differ). Version numbers are taken as max + 1; a clash with a concurrent save is a unique violation and the insert is simply tried again.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below), [3] source version id (text, checked as a UUID below)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the list query).
-- One row: the source version (only when it belongs to this job), the job, the current base CV and base
-- cover letter (as the Generate workflow reads them), and the names of every other job. When there is no
-- current analysed base CV, the base CV the version itself was written from is used. Facts are the effective
-- ones: Prayush's edited facts when there are any, else what was read from the file.
with p as (
  select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as jid,
         case when $3::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $3::text::uuid end as vid
),
j as (select jobs.* from jobs, p where jobs.id = p.jid and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid),
src as (
  select d.id, d.version_no, d.template_id, d.cv, d.cover_letter, d.reasons, d.review, d.keyword_coverage, d.base_cv_id
  from document_versions d, p, j
  where d.id = p.vid and d.job_id = j.id and d.owner_id = $1::uuid
),
cv as (
  select coalesce(edited_facts, structured) as structured from base_documents
  where owner_id = $1::uuid and kind = 'cv' and active and analysis_status = 'done' and not source_removed and structured is not null
  limit 1
),
cl as (
  select coalesce(edited_facts, structured) as structured from base_documents
  where owner_id = $1::uuid and kind = 'cover_letter' and active and analysis_status = 'done' and not source_removed and structured is not null
  limit 1
)
select exists (select 1 from j) as job_found,
  exists (select 1 from src) as version_found,
  (select to_jsonb(src) from src) as src,
  (select jsonb_build_object('title', j.title, 'employer', j.employer, 'advertiser', j.advertiser, 'rawText', coalesce(j.raw_text, '')) from j) as job,
  coalesce((select structured from cv),
           (select coalesce(b.edited_facts, b.structured) from base_documents b, src where b.id = src.base_cv_id and b.owner_id = $1::uuid and b.structured is not null)) as cv_structured,
  (select structured from cl) as cl_structured,
  coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('title', o.title, 'employer', o.employer, 'advertiser', o.advertiser)
                             order by o.created_at, o.id)
            from jobs o, j
            where o.owner_id = $1::uuid and o.id <> j.id
              and (o.title is not null or o.employer is not null or o.advertiser is not null)),
           '[]'::jsonb) as other_jobs;

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ before: { cv: $('Load edit inputs').first().json.src.cv, coverLetter: $('Load edit inputs').first().json.src.cover_letter }, after: { cv: $('Check edit request').first().json.cv, coverLetter: $('Check edit request').first().json.coverLetter } }) }}

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below), [3] source version id (text, checked as a UUID below),
-- [4] origin, [5] label (empty: Restored version N), [6] CV (JSON), [7] cover letter (JSON), [8] reasons (JSON),
-- [9] review (JSON), [10] checks (JSON) (each empty: copied from the source), [11] manual edit (true, false, or empty: copied)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the list query).
-- One new row, only when the source version belongs to this job. The version number is max + 1; two saves
-- at once can pick the same number, one then fails on the unique index (job, version number) and the
-- workflow runs this statement again.
with p as (
  select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as jid,
         case when $3::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $3::text::uuid end as vid
),
src as (
  select d.* from document_versions d, p
  where d.id = p.vid and d.job_id = p.jid and d.owner_id = $1::uuid
),
ins as (
  insert into document_versions (owner_id, job_id, run_id, version_no, label, base_cv_id, base_cv_hash,
                                 base_cover_letter_id, base_cover_letter_hash, template_id, cv, cover_letter,
                                 reasons, keyword_coverage, review, checks, instruction, manual_edit, origin, parent_version_id)
  select src.owner_id, src.job_id, null,
         (select coalesce(max(v.version_no), 0) + 1 from document_versions v where v.job_id = src.job_id),
         coalesce(nullif($5::text, ''), 'Restored version ' || src.version_no),
         src.base_cv_id, src.base_cv_hash, src.base_cover_letter_id, src.base_cover_letter_hash, src.template_id,
         coalesce(nullif($6::text, '')::jsonb, src.cv), coalesce(nullif($7::text, '')::jsonb, src.cover_letter),
         coalesce(nullif($8::text, '')::jsonb, src.reasons), src.keyword_coverage,
         coalesce(nullif($9::text, '')::jsonb, src.review), coalesce(nullif($10::text, '')::jsonb, src.checks),
         case when $4::text = 'restored' then src.instruction end,
         case $11::text when 'true' then true when 'false' then false else src.manual_edit end,
         $4::text, src.id
  from src
  returning id, version_no
)
select (select id from ins) as version_id, (select version_no from ins) as version_no,
       exists (select 1 from src) as found,
       exists (select 1 from jobs, p where jobs.id = p.jid and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid) as job_found;

parameters.content:
## Restore
`POST api/jobs/versions/restore?id=` body `{ versionId }`. Copies that version's documents, reasons, checks, review and keyword coverage into a **new** version: `origin restored`, label `Restored version N`, `parent_version_id` the restored one. The old row is not touched. `404 version_not_found` when the version is not this job's. Same retry on a version number clash as Edit.

parameters.query:
-- Parameters: [1] owner, [2] job id (text, checked as a UUID below), [3] source version id (text, checked as a UUID below),
-- [4] origin, [5] label (empty: Restored version N), [6] CV (JSON), [7] cover letter (JSON), [8] reasons (JSON),
-- [9] review (JSON), [10] checks (JSON) (each empty: copied from the source), [11] manual edit (true, false, or empty: copied)
-- Note: never write a dollar sign followed by a digit in SQL comments (see the list query).
-- One new row, only when the source version belongs to this job. The version number is max + 1; two saves
-- at once can pick the same number, one then fails on the unique index (job, version number) and the
-- workflow runs this statement again.
with p as (
  select case when $2::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $2::text::uuid end as jid,
         case when $3::text ~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' then $3::text::uuid end as vid
),
src as (
  select d.* from document_versions d, p
  where d.id = p.vid and d.job_id = p.jid and d.owner_id = $1::uuid
),
ins as (
  insert into document_versions (owner_id, job_id, run_id, version_no, label, base_cv_id, base_cv_hash,
                                 base_cover_letter_id, base_cover_letter_hash, template_id, cv, cover_letter,
                                 reasons, keyword_coverage, review, checks, instruction, manual_edit, origin, parent_version_id)
  select src.owner_id, src.job_id, null,
         (select coalesce(max(v.version_no), 0) + 1 from document_versions v where v.job_id = src.job_id),
         coalesce(nullif($5::text, ''), 'Restored version ' || src.version_no),
         src.base_cv_id, src.base_cv_hash, src.base_cover_letter_id, src.base_cover_letter_hash, src.template_id,
         coalesce(nullif($6::text, '')::jsonb, src.cv), coalesce(nullif($7::text, '')::jsonb, src.cover_letter),
         coalesce(nullif($8::text, '')::jsonb, src.reasons), src.keyword_coverage,
         coalesce(nullif($9::text, '')::jsonb, src.review), coalesce(nullif($10::text, '')::jsonb, src.checks),
         case when $4::text = 'restored' then src.instruction end,
         case $11::text when 'true' then true when 'false' then false else src.manual_edit end,
         $4::text, src.id
  from src
  returning id, version_no
)
select (select id from ins) as version_id, (select version_no from ins) as version_no,
       exists (select 1 from src) as found,
       exists (select 1 from jobs, p where jobs.id = p.jid and jobs.owner_id = $1::uuid) as job_found;
